audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Samson harvest visit, foxes/jackals, field burning, retaliatory killing, Judah surrender, jawbone battle, thirst, and judgeship notice, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for marital possession language, sister substitution, shualim animal term, arson damage, burning of Timnite woman and father, revenge chain, Judah's coerced surrender of Samson, jawbone wordplay and death number, water-place wording, and twenty-year notice.

verses.restored: After days, in days of wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat and said, I will go in to my wife, into chamber. But her father did not permit him to enter.

familiar.text: But it came to pass within a while after, in the time of wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a kid; and he said, I will go in to my wife into the chamber. But her father would not suffer him to go in.

modern.text: Later on, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife. “I want to go to my wife in her room,” he said. But her father would not let him enter.

original.text: וַיְהִ֨י מִיָּמִ֜ים בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּפְקֹ֨ד שִׁמְשׁ֤וֹן אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ בִּגְדִ֣י עִזִּ֔ים וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָבֹ֥אָה אֶל אִשְׁתִּ֖י הֶחָ֑דְרָה וְלֹֽא נְתָנ֥וֹ אָבִ֖יהָ לָבֽוֹא

verses.restored: Her father said, Saying, I said that hating, you hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Please let her be for you instead of her.

familiar.text: And her father said, I verily thought that thou hadst utterly hated her; therefore I gave her to thy companion: is not her younger sister fairer than she? take her, I pray thee, instead of her.

modern.text: “I was sure that you thoroughly hated her,” said her father, “so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֗יהָ אָמֹ֤ר אָמַ֨רְתִּי֙ כִּי שָׂנֹ֣א שְׂנֵאתָ֔הּ וָאֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה לְמֵרֵעֶ֑ךָ הֲלֹ֨א אֲחֹתָ֤הּ הַקְּטַנָּה֙ טוֹבָ֣ה מִמֶּ֔נָּה תְּהִי נָ֥א לְךָ֖ תַּחְתֶּֽיהָ

verses.restored: Samson said to them, This time I am clean/free of blame from Philistines when I do evil with them.

familiar.text: And Samson said concerning them, Now shall I be more blameless than the Philistines, though I do them a displeasure.

modern.text: Samson said to them, “This time I will be blameless in doing harm to the Philistines.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן נִקֵּ֥יתִי הַפַּ֖עַם מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים כִּֽי עֹשֶׂ֥ה אֲנִ֛י עִמָּ֖ם רָעָֽה

verses.restored: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes/jackals. He took torches, turned tail to tail, and put one torch between two tails in middle.

familiar.text: And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took firebrands, and turned tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst between two tails.

modern.text: Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. And he took torches, turned the foxes tail-to-tail, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן וַיִּלְכֹּ֖ד שְׁלֹשׁ מֵא֣וֹת שׁוּעָלִ֑ים וַיִּקַּ֣ח לַפִּדִ֗ים וַיֶּ֤פֶן זָנָב֙ אֶל זָנָ֔ב וַיָּ֨שֶׂם לַפִּ֥יד אֶחָ֛ד בֵּין שְׁנֵ֥י הַזְּנָב֖וֹת בַּתָּֽוֶךְ

verses.restored: He kindled fire in torches and sent them into standing grain of Philistines. He burned from stack to standing grain, and vineyard and olive grove.

familiar.text: And when he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burnt up both the shocks, and also the standing corn, with the vineyards and olives.

modern.text: Then he lit the torches and released the foxes into the standing grain of the Philistines, burning up the piles of grain and the standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.

original.text: וַיַּבְעֶר אֵשׁ֙ בַּלַּפִּידִ֔ים וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח בְּקָמ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּבְעֵ֛ר מִגָּדִ֥ישׁ וְעַד קָמָ֖ה וְעַד כֶּ֥רֶם זָֽיִת

verses.restored: Philistines said, Who did this? They said, Samson, son-in-law of Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion. Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire.

familiar.text: Then the Philistines said, Who hath done this? And they answered, Samson, the son in law of the Timnite, because he had taken his wife, and given her to his companion. And the Philistines came up, and burnt her and her father with fire.

modern.text: “Who did this?” the Philistines demanded. “It was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite,” they were told. “For his wife was given to his companion.” So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֮ מִ֣י עָ֣שָׂה זֹאת֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ חֲתַ֣ן הַתִּמְנִ֔י כִּ֚י לָקַ֣ח אֶת אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֖הּ לְמֵרֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיַּעֲל֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אוֹתָ֛הּ וְאֶת אָבִ֖יהָ בָּאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: Samson said to them, If you do such a thing, then I will take vengeance on you, and afterward I will stop.

familiar.text: And Samson said unto them, Though ye have done this, yet will I be avenged of you, and after that I will cease.

modern.text: And Samson told them, “Because you have done this, I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אִֽם תַּעֲשׂ֖וּן כָּזֹ֑את כִּ֛י אִם נִקַּ֥מְתִּי בָכֶ֖ם וְאַחַ֥ר אֶחְדָּֽל

verses.restored: He struck them leg upon thigh, a great blow. He went down and dwelt in cleft of rock of Etam.

familiar.text: And he smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter: and he went down and dwelt in the top of the rock Etam.

modern.text: And he struck them ruthlessly with a great slaughter, and then went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam.

original.text: וַיַּ֨ךְ אוֹתָ֥ם שׁ֛וֹק עַל יָרֵ֖ךְ מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיֵּ֣רֶד וַיֵּ֔שֶׁב בִּסְעִ֖יף סֶ֥לַע עֵיטָֽם

familiar.text: Then the Philistines went up, and pitched in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.

modern.text: Then the Philistines went up, camped in Judah, and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi.

original.text: וַיַּעֲל֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בִּיהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנָּטְשׁ֖וּ בַּלֶּֽחִי

verses.restored: Man of Judah said, Why have you come up against us? They said, To bind Samson we have come up, to do to him as he did to us.

familiar.text: And the men of Judah said, Why are ye come up against us? And they answered, To bind Samson are we come up, to do to him as he hath done to us.

modern.text: “Why have you attacked us?” said the men of Judah. The Philistines replied, “We have come to arrest Samson and pay him back for what he has done to us.”

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה לָמָ֖ה עֲלִיתֶ֣ם עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לֶאֱס֤וֹר אֶת שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ עָלִ֔ינוּ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת ל֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר עָ֥שָׂה לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: Three thousand men from Judah went down to cleft of rock of Etam and said to Samson, Do you not know that Philistines rule over us? What is this you have done to us? He said to them, As they did to me, so I did to them.

familiar.text: Then three thousand men of Judah went to the top of the rock Etam, and said to Samson, Knowest thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us? what is this that thou hast done unto us? And he said unto them, As they did unto me, so have I done unto them.

modern.text: In response, three thousand men of Judah went to the cave at the rock of Etam, and they asked Samson, “Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?” “I have done to them what they did to me,” he replied.

verses.restored: They said to him, To bind you we have come down, to give you into hand of Philistines. Samson said to them, Swear to me lest you yourselves strike me.

familiar.text: And they said unto him, We are come down to bind thee, that we may deliver thee into the hand of the Philistines. And Samson said unto them, Swear unto me, that ye will not fall upon me yourselves.

modern.text: But they said to him, “We have come down to arrest you and hand you over to the Philistines.” Samson replied, “Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.”

verses.restored: They said to him, saying, No; binding, we will bind you and give you into their hand, but putting to death, we will not put you to death. They bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.

familiar.text: And they spake unto him, saying, No; but we will bind thee fast, and deliver thee into their hand: but surely we will not kill thee. And they bound him with two new cords, and brought him up from the rock.

modern.text: “No,” they answered, “we will not kill you, but we will tie you up securely and hand you over to them.” So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.

modern.text: When Samson arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting against him. And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him. The ropes on his arms became like burnt flax, and the bonds broke loose from his hands.

familiar.text: And he was sore athirst, and called on the LORD, and said, Thou hast given this great deliverance into the hand of thy servant: and now shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?

modern.text: And being very thirsty, Samson cried out to the LORD, “You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”

verses.restored: Divine split open hollow that is at Lehi, and waters came out from it. He drank, his spirit returned, and he lived. Therefore its name was called En-hakkore, Spring of the Caller, which is at Lehi to this day.

familiar.text: But God clave an hollow place that was in the jaw, and there came water thereout; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived: wherefore he called the name thereof Enhakkore, which is in Lehi unto this day.

modern.text: So God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength returned, and he was revived. That is why he named it En-hakkore, and it remains in Lehi to this day.

modern.text: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֧ט אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בִּימֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה

translation_notes: The wife is still treated by father and husband as transferable possession. Her younger sister is proposed as a substitute and compared as 'better'; neither woman's consent is recorded.
Shualim may mean foxes or jackals. Jackals' pack behavior may fit the capture scene better, but the animal number and logistics remain folkloric or stylized.

Tying torches to animals and releasing them into fields depicts animal cruelty and agricultural arson. Grain, vineyards, and olive groves sustain whole communities, including people not responsible for the marriage conflict.

The Philistines burn the Timnite woman and her father—the very violence threatened in Judges 14. The text does not blame her; it exposes how patriarchal and collective retaliation consumes vulnerable people.
Samson repeatedly frames vengeance as limited—'afterward I will stop'—but retaliation generates another retaliation. Revenge does not close the cycle.
'Leg upon thigh' is an obscure idiom for a severe strike and should not be over-explained anatomically.
Judah acts under Philistine domination and hands Samson over to prevent wider attack. This is a coerced survival decision, not simple cowardice or ethnic betrayal.
The jawbone episode uses repeated lehi/hamor wordplay and an enormous death number. It is heroic folklore-shaped violence, not a reproducible spiritual model.
The Spirit formula does not authorize mass killing, improvised-weapon violence, or claims of invulnerability.
Samson's thirst makes his bodily vulnerability visible after his boast. The water-giving scene centers dependence and life rather than the kill count.
'Uncircumcised' remains ancient hostile boundary speech and cannot justify body shame or xenophobia.
safety_note: Do not glamorize arson, animal cruelty, mass killing, revenge, or improvised weapons. Do not blame Samson's wife for violence committed against her. The chapter's repeated measure-for-measure claims reveal escalating retaliation, not justice. Center civilians, food systems, animals, coerced communities, and the body that still needs water.
